A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same C2LIP study, with complete text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendix A. Pages 2–16 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance; the limited first-page changes do not impede comparison.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.5 and Appendix A report original C2LIP benchmark evaluations, component ablations, hyperparameter experiments, and LLaVA transfer results.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original benchmark, ablation, sensitivity, and visual instruction-tuning results in Section 4 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same noun-phrase concept extraction, parameter-free cross-modal attention pooling, auxiliary losses, and unchanged inference procedure.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is identical, including CC3M, compositionality and retrieval benchmarks, all 11 classification datasets in Table A6, and the LLaVA transfer experiments.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main and appendix tables, including SigLIP/CLIP controls, composition-aware and fine-grained methods, larger and multitask models, and LLaVA-SigLIP.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same model configuration, five-epoch training budget, preprocessing, accuracy and Recall@5 metrics. Section 4.5 retains the same LLaVA training and VQAScore evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: The loss-component ablation in Table 5, attention-map case studies in Figure 2, and hyperparameter sensitivity study in Table A2 are identical.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates and benchmark averages, without reported seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, C2LIP's average remains 75.0 in Table 2 and 76.7 across the classification benchmarks in Table A6.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and attention/loss formulations in Equations (1)–(8) are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: improving compositionality without hard-negative generation, maintaining strong general capabilities, and leaving inference cost unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of classification degradation through scene-centric representations remain unchanged, as do the limitations concerning final pooling and extension beyond object-attribute binding.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the code repository address and hyperlink target from SamsungLabs/concept_centric_clip to saic-fi/concept_centric_clip. Implementation, hyperparameter, and hardware disclosures are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether code availability improved.

R1.justification: Section 2, the positioning against prior approaches, and all 37 references are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 26 March 2026 to v2 dated 19 May 2026, alongside the repository-address edit. Scientific wording, terminology, and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The abstract has different line breaks and URL wrapping, and the marginal version stamp changes. All figures, tables, captions, and page layouts after page 1 are identical.

improvement.justification: The scientific argument, experimental evidence, appendices, and limitations are unchanged. The repository-address update and minor first-page formatting changes do not materially alter the paper's quality; the supplied PDFs do not demonstrate that an access problem was resolved.
